studies.Reference: Association of soy and fiber consumption with the risk of endometrial cancer.
studies.Authors: Goodman MT, Wilkens LR, Hankin JH, Lyu LC, Wu AH, Kolonel LN
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: All subjects were interviewed using a diet history questionnaire that included over 250 food items.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: High consumption of soy products and other legumes was associated with a decreased risk of endometrial cancer
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: to examine the role of dietary soy, fiber, and related foods and nutrients on the risk of endometrial cancer
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: High consumption of soy products and other legumes

studies.Reference: The association between dietary intake and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or higher among women in a high-risk rural area of China.
studies.Authors: Feng CY, Lin M, Lakhaney D, Sun HK, Dai XB, Zhao FH, Qiao YL
studies.Design: Cross-Sectional (with case-control analysis among HPV-positive women)
studies.Stage: CIN2+ (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or higher, including CIN2, CIN3, and cancer)
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Dietary food intake information was collected by a 79-item Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ).

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 748 HPV-positive women ... were included in our data analysis.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: legumes ... yielded adjusted odds ratios (ORs) of ... 0.591 (95% CI, 0.392–0.892; P for trend = 0.012)

headline.funnel_interpretation: Insufficient studies to perform formal publication bias testing.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.58 (95% CI: 0.42–0.79), suggesting that legumes is associated with a lower risk of uterine cancer. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.
